overview: This file consists of a 17 November 1934 despatch from the American Consul General in Tokyo transmitting English translations of two colonial Taiwan regulations concerning the admission, registration, residence, surveillance, and deportation of aliens. The first regulation, issued in February 1918, establishes grounds for refusing entry, passport and visa requirements, police examination, and exemptions for diplomats, officials, and ships’ crews. The second, issued in July 1899, requires reports by foreign residents, lodgers, landlords, and hotelkeepers; creates police registers of foreigners; authorizes deportation; and prescribes fines and imprisonment. Both translated regulations appear twice in the file, apparently as duplicate or carbon copies, with substantial OCR corruption in the second set.

people.name: C. Matsuo
people.role: Interpreter and translator of the enclosed regulations

subfiles.title: Despatch from Arthur Garrels transmitting Taiwan alien regulations
subfiles.about: The Consul General forwards translations of Taiwan’s rules governing the admission and temporary residence of aliens.
subfiles.summary: Garrels responds to the Department’s instruction requesting special immigration reports and supplements earlier Consulate General reports. He encloses translations obtained from the American Vice Consul at Taihoku, noting that Taiwan’s regulations differ from those in Japan proper. The Vice Consul understood the rules to apply equally to temporary visitors and aliens entering for gainful employment, with no special restrictions on the latter group.

subfiles.title: Translation of Taiwan Government Order No. 7 on the landing of foreigners
subfiles.about: The order specifies passport requirements and the grounds on which colonial authorities may refuse entry to or deport a foreigner.
subfiles.summary: The regulation permits refusal of landing to foreigners lacking valid documents or considered threats to imperial interests, public order, morals, or public health, as well as beggars, habitual loafers, mentally incapacitated persons, and likely public charges. It requires passports or nationality certificates bearing photographs and recent Japanese diplomatic or consular visas, subject to reciprocal exemptions. Foreigners must answer police questions truthfully, while fraud or misuse of documents can lead to exclusion and deportation. Diplomats, consular personnel, official travelers, their families, and crews of foreign vessels are exempted.

subfiles.title: Regulations Concerning Treatment of Aliens, Taiwan Government General Order No. 71
subfiles.about: The regulation establishes police reporting and registration requirements for foreigners residing or lodging in Taiwan and provides penalties and deportation powers.
subfiles.summary: Hosts, landlords, and hotelkeepers must report a foreign lodger’s identity, nationality, occupation, movements, and other particulars to the police, while longer-term foreign residents must register themselves, their families, and attendants. Police maintain a Register of Foreigners, which may be inspected or copied for a fee, and foreigners must answer questions and produce proof of nationality. The Governor General may deport indigent persons, wanderers, beggars, threats to public order or morals, and persons who return after deportation. Noncompliance, false reports, or failure to depart can bring fines or imprisonment, while Chinese residents are partly exempted or governed by separate regulations.

subfiles.title: Duplicate translation of Taiwan Government Order No. 7
subfiles.about: This is a duplicate, more heavily OCR-corrupted copy of the regulation governing the landing and exclusion of foreigners.
subfiles.summary: The duplicate repeats the grounds for excluding foreigners, including inadequate documentation, threats to imperial interests or public order, disease, indigence, and other conditions thought likely to create a public burden. It restates the passport, photograph, visa, police-questioning, fraud, and deportation provisions. It also preserves the exemptions for foreign diplomatic and consular personnel, official travelers, their families, and foreign ships’ crews.

subfiles.title: Duplicate translation of Taiwan Government General Order No. 71
subfiles.about: This duplicate copy restates Taiwan’s reporting, registration, policing, deportation, and penalty provisions for aliens.
subfiles.summary: The text repeats the obligations of lodging providers and foreign residents to report personal information, residence, departure, removal, and other census-related events to the police. It covers maintenance and public inspection of the Register of Foreigners, production of passports, and police questioning. Deportation is authorized for indigence, wandering, begging, threats to order or morals, and unauthorized re-entry, with fines or imprisonment for violations. The closing attribution identifies C. Matsuo as the interpreter, although the consular office and place-name are badly corrupted by OCR.

interest: The file provides a compact view of the legal machinery used to monitor foreigners in Japanese colonial Taiwan, combining border exclusion with detailed local police registration and household reporting. Particularly useful are the distinctions between Taiwan and Japan proper, the reciprocal approach to passport and visa requirements, the exemptions for diplomats and ships’ crews, and the separate legal treatment of Chinese residents. The duplicate enclosures also offer an unusually clear demonstration of OCR corruption, since the better readings in one copy can be used to reconstruct damaged passages in the other.
